name: Maine
summary: Maine allows plug-in solar up to 1,200 watts in two tiers: up to 420 watts you can install yourself, and anything larger needs a licensed electrician.

tiers.rule: Must be installed by a licensed electrician, and reported to your utility within 30 days.

certification: Reported to reference UL 3700, the plug-in solar safety standard.

utility.notification: Systems over 420 W: notify the utility within 30 days of installing. Sources disagree on whether smaller systems must also notify.
utility.fees: Utilities may not require pre-approval, an interconnection application, or fees.

renters: Not addressed in the sources we found. Ask your landlord in writing.
hoa: Not addressed in the sources we found.
open_questions: Effective date is reported as July 14, 15, or 29, 2026 depending on the source. We show July 15.
Whether the 30-day utility notice also applies to systems of 420 W or less.
The exact certification wording needs checking against the chaptered law.

sources.title: PV Tech: Maine passes balcony solar law
